scope: Dates bound monument phases represented in this collection, not the lifespan or territorial extent of a polity. Historical context does not prove construction patronage.

empires.name: Vijayanagara Empire
empires.summary: Courtly and sacred building at Hampi
empires.history: Temple precincts, pillared halls and royal enclosures coexist in the capital landscape. A Vijayanagara phase can be an enlargement of a much older sacred site. In the collection: Developed under Vijayanagara patronage, the complex forms part of Hampi's sacred landscape. Its buildings reflect successive phases rather than a single construction event.
empires.architectural_notes: Vitthala Temple: An enclosure brings together the main shrine, pillared halls and the chariot-shaped shrine. Architectural details reward close inspection of individual pillars and pavilions. Virupaksha Temple: Two main courts divide the rectangular enclosure. Gateway towers establish the approach to the shrine and its pillared spaces. Achyutaraya Temple: Two precinct walls frame courtyards and gateway towers. A vestibule and assembly hall connect the sanctuary with the larger mandapa.

empires.name: Early Chalukyas of Badami
empires.summary: Experimentation in structural and rock-cut temples
empires.history: Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal preserve varied shrine forms. Northern and southern architectural vocabularies occur within this regional collection. In the collection: The temple commemorates the military success of Lokamahadevi's husband. Its location within the Pattadakal ensemble makes it a useful point of comparison with neighbouring temple forms.
empires.architectural_notes: Virupaksha Temple: The southern architectural tradition is expressed in the temple's shrine and superstructure. Sculpture is integral to its architectural treatment. Badami Cave 3: A pillared entrance space leads into the excavated interior. Large relief panels and carved bracket figures are important parts of the architectural experience. Durga Temple: A rounded shrine end and surrounding passage distinguish the plan. An open colonnade, hall and porch establish a sequence between the exterior and the shrine.

empires.name: Hoysala dynasty
empires.history: Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura represent distinct commissions. Shared craftsmanship does not make their patrons or construction dates identical. In the collection: Worship at the Belur temple is documented from 1117 CE. It belongs to the UNESCO-listed Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas and remains an active religious place.
empires.architectural_notes: Chennakeshava Temple: The circumambulatory platform allows the exterior to be experienced as a sequence of carved surfaces. The present form also reflects changes and losses over time. Hoysaleswara Temple: Two sanctuaries, for Hoysaleswara and Shantaleswara, form the temple composition. A raised platform follows the articulated outline, while turned pillars and ornamented ceilings distinguish the interior. Keshava Temple: Three shrines form a trikuta arrangement on a raised, star-shaped platform. Horizontal sculptural bands animate the outer walls, while the platform supports movement around the temple.

empires.name: Chola Empire
empires.region: Tamil Nadu and the Kaveri region
empires.history: The three Great Living Chola Temples represent successive royal commissions. Their continued ritual use and later repairs are separate from their initial building phases. In the collection: The temple is associated with Rajaraja I and the early eleventh-century Chola state. It remains part of a living religious tradition; painting, sculpture and stone construction complement the monumental sanctuary tower.
empires.architectural_notes: Brihadisvara Temple: The tall pyramidal vimana dominates a broad enclosed court. Gateways and subsidiary structures establish an axial approach to the sanctuary. Airavatesvara Temple: The sanctuary tower and richly articulated mandapa form the main composition. Chariot-like sculptural treatment and finely worked supports distinguish its ceremonial spaces. Brihadisvara Temple, Gangaikonda Cholapuram: The shrine rises into a tiered vimana. Sculpture is integrated into the exterior niches and the main axis includes a pillared hall.

sources.title: Brihadisvara Temple — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Pallava dynasty
empires.history: The monuments at Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram preserve different building techniques and temple forms within Pallava-period traditions. In the collection: The Shore Temple belongs to the Pallava architectural landscape at Mahabalipuram. Unlike the group’s rock-cut caves and monolithic rathas, it represents structural temple building beside the sea.
empires.architectural_notes: Shore Temple: Two prominent tiered towers and associated shrines occupy a compact coastal precinct. Nandi figures along the enclosure reinforce the shrine ensemble’s sculptural setting. Kailasanatha Temple, Kanchipuram: A tiered shrine rises inside an enclosure lined with smaller shrines. A narrow passage permits circulation around the sanctum.

sources.title: Shore Temple — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Mughal Empire
empires.history: The collection connects monumental tombs, fortified precincts, mosques and gardens. Named patronage is retained where documented; a stylistic association alone is historical context. In the collection: Shah Jahan commissioned the mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal beside the Yamuna. UNESCO distinguishes the main tomb’s completion in 1648 from later ancillary works completed in 1653; its descriptions also use different starting years, so this record retains that uncertainty.
empires.architectural_notes: Taj Mahal: The tomb stands on a raised terrace beyond a formally divided garden. Four minarets frame the central domed building, while subsidiary structures and a monumental entrance organize the approach. Agra Fort: Fortified gates lead into successive courts and palace precincts. The Jahangiri Mahal, Khas Mahal and audience halls should be read as distinct components within the larger enclosure. Fatehpur Sikri: The complex includes palaces, public audience spaces, columned pavilions and a mosque precinct. Levels and courtyards separate public circulation from more restricted royal spaces.

sources.title: Taj Mahal — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Delhi Sultanate
empires.history: The Qutb ensemble and the later political use of Daulatabad illustrate different aspects of the sultanate's built environment. Control of a fort is distinct from its original construction. In the collection: The minaret forms part of a larger early Sultanate ensemble at Mehrauli. Successive construction and repair phases shaped the tower now visible; nearby mosques, tombs and gateways belong to the complex but are not interchangeable with the minaret itself.
empires.architectural_notes: Qutb Minar: The circular tower narrows upward through successive storeys. Alternating fluted surfaces, inscription bands and projecting balconies articulate the elevation. Daulatabad Fort: Successive fortified enclosures, gateways, a moat and a steep citadel exploit the isolated hill's terrain.

sources.title: Qutb Minar — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Rashtrakuta dynasty
empires.history: Ellora's Kailasa shrine provides a documented setting for studying an excavated architectural ensemble and its sculptural surfaces. In the collection: Kailasa is the major monolithic Hindu temple within Ellora’s multi-religious cave complex. Excavation removed surrounding basalt to create courts, built-looking forms and sculptural surfaces from the parent rock.
empires.architectural_notes: Kailasa Temple, Ellora: A deep open court surrounds the main temple mass. Gateways, subsidiary spaces and relief-covered walls create a sequence that differs from a cave simply cut into a cliff face.

sources.title: Kailasa Temple, Ellora — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Kakatiya dynasty
empires.history: Ramappa and the Thousand Pillar Temple document different Kakatiya-period commissions, with substantial attention to columns, raised bases and shrine arrangements. In the collection: The Rudreshwara temple at Palampet was commissioned in the Kakatiya period. UNESCO dates the beginning of its construction to 1213.
empires.architectural_notes: Ramappa Temple: A raised platform carries the main shrine and pillared hall. Carved brackets and a lightweight brick superstructure are among the documented details. Thousand Pillar Temple: The temple's three-shrine arrangement, sculpted columns and raised platform organize a compact ritual ensemble.

sources.title: Ramappa Temple
sources.locator: Outstanding Universal Value, construction and materials

sources.title: Thousand Pillar Temple — history and architecture

empires.name: Qutb Shahi dynasty
empires.history: Golconda, Charminar and the royal tombs connect defence, urban identity and funerary architecture. Each record retains its own date and evidence. In the collection: The Hyderabad district account dates the monument to 1591 under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. Several explanations for its commemoration survive; the record does not turn an uncertain founding story into an established fact.
empires.architectural_notes: Charminar: Four large arches define passages through the square structure. Corner minarets, balconies and upper-level spaces mark the monument’s relationship to the surrounding streets. Golconda Fort: The granite hill carries the upper citadel. Successive lines of walls, gateways and bastions control access to the interior. Qutb Shahi Tombs: Domed tombs rise on platforms and often use repeated arches to articulate their elevations.

sources.title: Charminar — historical and architectural reference
sources.publisher: Official heritage, tourism or monument-management authority

sources.title: The Qutb Shahi Monuments of Hyderabad

empires.name: Gujarat Sultanate
empires.summary: Mosques, stone screens and regional craftsmanship
empires.history: Champaner and Ahmedabad preserve distinct mosque ensembles. Gujarat's architecture also reflects local patrons and craftspeople beyond any one ruling house. In the collection: The congregational mosque belongs to the Gujarat Sultanate phase of Champaner. The park preserves the mosque alongside the fortified capital and earlier remains.
empires.architectural_notes: Jami Masjid, Champaner: Two slender minarets flank the central entrance and an open courtyard leads to the prayer hall. Sidi Saiyyed Mosque: The open façade is articulated by arches. Carved stone screens fill windows in the rear wall. Adalaj Stepwell: Multiple subterranean levels descend toward the well through carved columns, landings and an octagonal opening.

sources.title: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
sources.locator: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, architecture and jalis

empires.name: Malwa Sultanate
empires.history: Mandu's palace landscape brings together water, courts and vaulted spaces. The archive's association is restricted to the monument evidence linked below. In the collection: The Dhar district account attributes the palace to Ghiyasuddin Khalji. An architectural survey proposes the earlier reign of Mahmud Khalji I. The date range reflects both attributions.
empires.architectural_notes: Jahaz Mahal, Mandu: A long double-storey range with terraces and roof pavilions extends between the Munj and Kapur tanks.

empires.name: Adil Shahi dynasty
empires.history: Gol Gumbaz connects an immense domed chamber with a specific royal funerary setting. It is not a label for every later monument in Karnataka. In the collection: Gol Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur. The domed chamber contains the Whispering Gallery around its interior.
empires.architectural_notes: Gol Gumbaz: A large dome crowns the square chamber, and four corner towers contain stairs to the upper level.

empires.name: Ahom kingdom
empires.summary: Royal pavilions, temples and burial landscapes
empires.history: Rang Ghar, Shiva Dol and the Moidams show different royal and sacred functions. The burial landscape developed over many generations. In the collection: The Assam district account places the Shivadol, Vishnudol and Devidol beside the tank in 1734 under Queen Madambika. This record concerns the Shiva temple, not every structure at the larger water precinct.
empires.architectural_notes: Shiva Dol: A rising sanctuary tower gives the temple a strong vertical profile. Its relationship to the tank and adjoining shrines is an important part of the setting. Rang Ghar: A two-storeyed, elongated pavilion uses repeated openings and a curved roof profile to face the surrounding ground. Charaideo Moidams: Earth-covered burial vaults, small shrines and enclosing walls form a funerary landscape integrated with the terrain.

sources.title: Shiva Dol — historical and architectural reference
sources.publisher: Official heritage, tourism or monument-management authority

empires.name: Maratha polity
empires.history: Hill, coastal and island forts adapted defence to terrain. Maratha occupation or strengthening need not establish the earliest construction date of a fort. In the collection: Shivaji adapted the earlier hill fort as a Maratha capital and held his coronation there in 1674. Its history includes earlier occupation and later military events.
empires.architectural_notes: Raigad Fort: Gateways and defensive walls guard approaches to palace platforms, courts and other summit remains. Sindhudurg Fort: Masonry ramparts and bastions follow the island's edge, enclosing internal buildings and protected landing approaches. Gingee Fort: Three fortified hills, connecting walls, gateways and water-storage works form a defensive landscape.

empires.name: Portuguese administration in India
empires.history: Goa's churches and Diu's fort belong to different religious and military settings under Portuguese administration. Communities and institutions also exercised patronage. In the collection: The basilica is a component of Goa’s World Heritage churches and convents and houses the tomb associated with Francis Xavier. Its early modern architecture belongs to the wider exchange of European religious forms in Portuguese Asia.
empires.architectural_notes: Basilica of Bom Jesus: An articulated façade uses Classical architectural orders. The longitudinal church interior and associated funerary setting should be distinguished from the larger Old Goa group. Se Cathedral: A long church plan with chapels and a monumental facade opens onto Old Goa's ecclesiastical precinct. Diu Fort: Massive coastal ramparts, bastions and landward defences enclose an eastern promontory of the island.

sources.title: Basilica of Bom Jesus — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: British colonial administration
empires.history: Railway, civic and penal buildings served different colonial functions. Their designers, patrons and users should be studied separately rather than flattened into one architectural style. In the collection: The memorial belongs to the early twentieth century and now functions as a museum. Its monumental composition combines European Classical and Renaissance references with Indian architectural elements; it broadens the archive beyond ancient and medieval monuments.
empires.architectural_notes: Victoria Memorial: A central dome organizes a symmetrical memorial building. Subsidiary domed forms, colonnaded approaches and formal gardens create the larger civic composition. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus: The central dome anchors a symmetrical façade articulated by towers, gables and pointed openings. Gateway of India: A tall central opening faces the harbour, framed by projecting towers and a central dome.

sources.title: Victoria Memorial — historical and architectural reference
sources.publisher: Official heritage, tourism or monument-management authority

sources.title: Cellular Jail
sources.locator: Description, radial plan and National Memorial

empires.name: Indus / Harappan civilisation
empires.region: Gujarat and the wider Indus world
empires.history: Lothal and Dholavira support comparison of urban planning, water systems and archaeological interpretation. This is a civilisation, not a securely identified imperial dynasty. In the collection: Dholavira preserves a long sequence of Harappan occupation. The mapped ruins include multiple divisions of the settlement and its engineered system for water storage.
empires.architectural_notes: Dholavira Harappan City: The fortified sectors and reservoirs reflect the site's response to seasonal water supply in an arid landscape. Lothal Archaeological Site: Excavated brick platforms, drains, domestic areas and a large basin reveal aspects of settlement planning.

sources.title: Lothal Archaeological Site — history and architecture

empires.name: Bundela rulers
empires.history: Orchha and Datia connect palace architecture to Bundela patrons. Differing reported dates remain visible rather than being reduced to false precision. In the collection: Jahangir Mahal is associated with the Bundela ruler Bir Singh Deo. It forms part of the palace ensemble in Orchha's fortified river setting.
empires.architectural_notes: Jahangir Mahal, Orchha: Ranges enclose a central courtyard, with domed pavilions marking the corners and upper silhouette. Datia Palace: A compact, multi-storeyed mass of rooms, courts and roof pavilions rises above a rocky foundation.

sources.title: Jahangir Mahal, Orchha
sources.locator: Description of palace plans and fort complex

empires.name: Kullu kingdom
empires.history: Hadimba's surviving shrine is associated with Bahadur Singh. Local sacred tradition and the date of the surviving building are recorded separately. In the collection: Bahadur Singh commissioned the surviving shrine in 1553. The sanctuary encloses a natural rock associated with local worship; epic traditions are not treated as construction dates.
empires.architectural_notes: Hadimba Devi Temple: A timber superstructure rises above a stone base, with tiers of pitched roofs and carved entrance members.

sources.title: Hadimba Devi Temple — history and architecture

empires.name: Guge kingdom
empires.history: Tabo's foundation is associated with western Tibetan royal patronage. The monastic compound also contains later phases. In the collection: The monastery was founded in 996 under western Tibetan royal patronage. Its painted interiors and later buildings represent several phases, rather than one unchanged tenth-century structure.
empires.architectural_notes: Tabo Monastery: Low earthen buildings enclose temple rooms and monastic spaces. Murals and modelled figures form important parts of the interiors.

empires.name: Sikh Empire
empires.history: The collection includes sacred architecture and additions to an earlier fort. Ranjit Singh's period of patronage does not establish the first foundation of every site. In the collection: The fort passed from the Bhangi Misl to Maharaja Ranjit Singh and later British control. Sikh-period strengthening is recorded as an addition, not as the first construction of every wall.
empires.architectural_notes: Gobindgarh Fort: Defensive walls, bastions, gateways and interior courts organize a lowland military enclosure.

empires.name: Utpala dynasty
empires.history: Avantivarman's Avantiswami precinct survives as a ruined temple ensemble. Its colonnaded setting and carved fragments retain evidence of a specific ninth-century commission. In the collection: Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty commissioned the ninth-century shrine. The record concentrates on the Avantiswami precinct rather than treating nearby temples as one building.
empires.architectural_notes: Avantiswami Temple: A central sanctuary platform stands within a rectangular, colonnaded enclosure. Carved architectural fragments survive around the ruined court.

empires.name: Koch kingdom
empires.history: Kamakhya's major sixteenth-century rebuilding is linked to Naranarayan. Earlier sacred origins and later additions are separate phases. In the collection: The shrine has earlier origins and repeated rebuilding. Koch ruler Naranarayan is associated with the major sixteenth-century reconstruction; later additions form part of its layered history.
empires.architectural_notes: Kamakhya Temple: The sanctuary and adjoining halls combine a rounded roof profile with carved external surfaces on Nilachal Hill.

empires.name: Jaintia kingdom
empires.history: Nartiang's shrine is associated with Jaintia religious history. A precise building date or a named commissioner for every current part has not been established here. In the collection: The Durga shrine is associated with Jaintia religious history. Sources describe centuries of worship, but a precise date for the photographed structure is not established here.
empires.architectural_notes: Nartiang Durga Temple: A roofed shrine and covered worship spaces retain a distinct hill-region setting. Timber members and the pitched roof are prominent visible elements.

sources.title: Nartiang Durga Temple — history and architecture

empires.date_label: Dates vary by documented monument phase

empires.name: Kingdom of Manipur
empires.history: Kangla functioned as a seat of Manipuri rulers until 1891. Its changing sacred and royal structures represent more than one construction phase. In the collection: Kangla was the seat of Manipuri rulers until 1891. The palace precinct contains remains and renewed sacred structures; its traditional foundation chronology is not used as the date of every building.
empires.architectural_notes: Kangla Fort: Moats, gateways, temples and open grounds define a large fortified royal landscape in the centre of Imphal.
empires.date_label: Dates vary by documented monument phase

empires.name: Manikya rulers of Tripura
empires.history: Ujjayanta and Neermahal represent different modern princely commissions. Unakoti's much earlier reliefs are not assigned to these rulers. In the collection: Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya commissioned the palace in 1899–1901. It later accommodated the state legislature and now serves as a museum.
empires.architectural_notes: Ujjayanta Palace: A domed central block and wings face formal gardens and pools. Ornamental rooms include crafted wooden ceilings. Neermahal: The palace occupies an island in Rudrasagar Lake, with arcaded elevations and pavilion-like roof elements facing the water.

empires.name: Dimasa Kachari kingdom
empires.summary: The former royal landscape of Dimapur
empires.history: Dimapur's carved pillars are connected to the Kachari landscape. Their exact dates and functions remain uncertain. In the collection: The site is associated with the Dimasa Kachari kingdom. Official and secondary summaries differ on dates, and the original purpose of the sculpted pillars is uncertain.
empires.architectural_notes: Kachari Rajbari Ruins: Rows of freestanding carved stone pillars survive within a former royal enclosure; a brick gateway belongs to the wider remains.

sources.title: Kachari Rajbari Ruins — history and architecture

empires.date_label: Dates vary by documented monument phase

empires.name: Namgyal kingdom of Sikkim
empires.history: Rabdentse's period as a capital and the expansion of Pemayangtse represent different relationships between royalty and buildings. In the collection: Founded as an early religious establishment, the monastery was enlarged under Sikkim's Chogyal rulers. Sources distinguish its seventeenth-century beginnings from eighteenth-century expansion.
empires.architectural_notes: Pemayangtse Monastery: A principal temple and associated monastic buildings contain painted and carved interiors above a hillside court. Rabdentse Palace Ruins: Ruined palace walls, platforms, courts and chortens occupy a ridge near Pemayangtse monastery.

empires.name: Chutiya kingdom
empires.history: The tourism account associates Malinithan's medieval phase with Chutiya rulers. This remains a qualified attribution rather than an independently verified named commission. In the collection: The archaeological site preserves a medieval temple and sculptural remains. Arunachal Tourism associates the phase with Chutiya rulers; this is a qualified historical attribution.
empires.architectural_notes: Malinithan Temple Ruins: Carved stone fragments, column members and a raised temple platform survive within the archaeological precinct.

sources.title: Malinithan Temple Ruins — history and architecture

empires.name: Palian chiefs
empires.history: Sibuta Lung is associated with the chief Sibuta and local oral traditions. It is a memorial stone, not an imperial palace or an enclosed building. In the collection: The memorial is associated with the Palian chief Sibuta at Tachhip. Accounts of its erection belong partly to oral tradition, and no precise construction year is imposed here.
empires.architectural_notes: Sibuta Lung: A tall upright stone forms the commemorative focus. It is recorded as a memorial monument rather than a building with enclosed rooms.
empires.date_label: Dates vary by documented monument phase

empires.name: Nagavanshi rulers of Kawardha
empires.history: Bhoramdeo provides the collection's regional example. These rulers are not conflated with the Nagvanshi house of Chotanagpur. In the collection: The main stone Shiva shrine forms part of a group that also includes earlier and later monuments. Its medieval architecture is associated with the region's Nagavanshi rulers.
empires.architectural_notes: Bhoramdeo Temple: A raised sanctuary and hall carry richly carved external surfaces beneath a rising shrine tower.

empires.name: Panduvamshis of Dakshina Kosala
empires.history: Queen Vasata's Lakshmana temple provides a documented example within Sirpur's wider religious landscape. In the collection: Queen Vasata commissioned the Vishnu shrine in memory of Harshagupta in the Panduvamshi period. It belongs to Sirpur's wider, multi-religious archaeological landscape.
empires.architectural_notes: Lakshmana Temple, Sirpur: A brick sanctuary tower rises above the temple platform. Decorated brick surfaces and a carved stone doorway distinguish the surviving structure.

sources.title: Lakshmana Temple, Sirpur — history and architecture

empires.name: Baj Basanta patron family
empires.history: Maluti's small temples represent successive family patronage. A shared village setting does not turn them into one construction campaign. In the collection: The village's patron families sponsored successive temples rather than one unified royal palace. Sources associate the temple-building tradition with the Baj Basanta family.
empires.architectural_notes: Maluti Temples: Clusters of small brick temples carry terracotta reliefs and different roof profiles, with narrow spaces between individual shrines.

empires.name: Nagvanshis of Chotanagpur
empires.history: Ranchi's Jagannath temple records a seventeenth-century foundation. Its later reconstruction is distinct from the original commission. In the collection: The original hilltop shrine was founded in the seventeenth century under local Nagvanshi patronage. Parts of the present building reflect reconstruction after a twentieth-century collapse.
empires.architectural_notes: Jagannath Temple, Ranchi: A raised approach leads to the temple and its prominent curving tower, with halls and associated spaces around the sanctuary.

sources.title: Jagannath Temple, Ranchi — history and architecture

empires.name: Sur dynasty
empires.history: Sher Shah's tomb combines an octagonal plan, lake setting and causeway. The dated funerary commission is separate from the ruler's wider political career. In the collection: Sher Shah Suri's mausoleum was completed in 1545 during the Sur dynasty. Its commemorative function and completion are distinguished from the emperor's earlier political career.
empires.architectural_notes: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri: An octagonal domed tomb stands on a platform in an artificial lake, connected to land by a stone causeway.

sources.title: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri — history and architecture

empires.name: Nawabs of Bengal
empires.history: Hazarduari was commissioned by Humayun Jah and designed by Duncan MacLeod. European architectural vocabulary does not make the British state its patron. In the collection: Nawab Humayun Jah commissioned the palace, designed by Duncan MacLeod. Its European architectural vocabulary does not erase the agency of its Nawabi patron.
empires.architectural_notes: Hazarduari Palace: A long classical facade, prominent entrance steps and repeated columns face the Nizamat precinct. Interior rooms now accommodate museum collections.

empires.name: Somavamshi period
empires.history: Mukteshwar is associated with the architectural context of tenth-century Odisha. A dynastic-period label is not evidence for a named royal commissioner. In the collection: The tenth-century Shiva shrine occupies an important place in the development of Odisha temple architecture. A dynastic-period association is not treated as proof of a named commissioner.
empires.architectural_notes: Mukteshwar Temple: A decorated arched torana introduces the shrine enclosure, while the sanctuary tower and hall display carved stone ornament.

empires.name: Paramara dynasty
empires.history: Bhojeshwar is associated with Bhoja. Its unfinished fabric and adjacent architectural traces make construction process part of the heritage story. In the collection: The unfinished Shiva temple is associated with Paramara ruler Bhoja. Nearby quarry marks and architectural drawings are important evidence of its construction process.
empires.architectural_notes: Bhojeshwar Temple: An enormous sanctuary chamber and massive pillars stand on a raised platform; unfinished work remains visible.

empires.name: Gupta period
empires.history: Deogarh's Vishnu temple is a period association. The record does not identify a securely documented named royal commissioner. In the collection: The Vishnu shrine belongs to the Gupta-period architectural tradition. Its surviving reliefs and platform are early evidence of a developed structural temple plan.
empires.architectural_notes: Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh: A square sanctuary stands on a raised platform, with sculptural panels on its outer walls and remains of subsidiary shrines.

sources.title: Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh — history and architecture

empires.name: Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri
empires.history: Devagiri's early fortified phase precedes later sultanate control and the name Daulatabad. Later political use is recorded as a separate relationship. In the collection: The Yadava stronghold became the Delhi Sultanate's capital during Muhammad bin Tughluq's fourteenth-century transfer. Later Deccan rulers adapted the extensive defences.
empires.architectural_notes: Daulatabad Fort: Successive fortified enclosures, gateways, a moat and a steep citadel exploit the isolated hill's terrain.

empires.name: Keladi / Ikkeri Nayakas
empires.history: Kerala Tourism associates Bekal's principal phase with Shivappa Nayaka of Ikkeri. The connection is restricted to this documented phase. In the collection: Kerala Tourism associates the fort's principal construction with Shivappa Nayaka of Ikkeri. Later control by Mysore belongs to a separate historical phase.
empires.architectural_notes: Bekal Fort: Coastal ramparts, bastions and an observation position occupy a headland above the Arabian Sea.

empires.name: Rathore rulers of Bikaner
empires.summary: Lowland forts and successive palace interiors
empires.history: Rai Singh's Junagarh fort became the core of a palace ensemble enlarged by later rulers. Initial walls and later decorated rooms need separate dates. In the collection: Raja Rai Singh's fort became the core of a palace ensemble enlarged by later Bikaner rulers. The dates describe the initial fort phase, not every decorated room.
empires.architectural_notes: Junagarh Fort: Defensive walls enclose successive courts, palaces and projecting windows on a lowland site.

empires.name: French administration in India
empires.history: The Sacred Heart church was built in French-administered Pondicherry. This is political context, not a claim that the French state commissioned it. In the collection: The Catholic church developed in the early twentieth century in French-administered Pondicherry. Its religious patronage is distinguished from a claim that the French state commissioned the building.
empires.architectural_notes: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus: A strongly articulated facade and pointed openings introduce the church, whose stained-glass panels form a notable part of its interior.

sources.title: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus — history and architecture

empires.name: Chandella dynasty
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple: The temple belongs to the Chandella architectural flowering at Khajuraho. Its sculptural program is integral to the architecture, while the clustered sanctuary towers create a rising composition rather than a single isolated vertical mass.
empires.architectural_notes: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple: An elevated platform supports a sequence of halls leading toward the sanctuary. Curved towers and smaller associated spires emphasize the inner sacred space.

sources.title: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Eastern Ganga dynasty
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Sun Temple, Konark: The temple expresses the solar deity Surya’s chariot through architectural scale, carved wheels and sculptural programs. The thirteenth-century ensemble survives incompletely, so remaining halls and sculptures should not be mistaken for the original complete temple. Jagannath Temple, Puri: The present principal shrine is associated with the Eastern Ganga dynasty. Its construction belongs to the twelfth century and the complex remains in ritual use.
empires.architectural_notes: Sun Temple, Konark: Carved chariot wheels articulate the raised base. Monumental surviving masses, subsidiary remains and sculptural bands reveal the original ceremonial composition. Jagannath Temple, Puri: An elevated platform carries the main curving tower and the sequence of halls on its ceremonial axis.

sources.title: Sun Temple, Konark — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Chaulukya / Solanki dynasty
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Sun Temple, Modhera: Gujarat Tourism, citing ASI, places construction in 1026–1027 under Bhima I. The ensemble combines solar devotion with a highly articulated reservoir and halls, rather than presenting only an isolated sanctuary. Rani-ki-Vav: The eleventh-century stepwell was conceived as a memorial and as a carefully designed water structure. UNESCO interprets it as an inverted temple, with multiple descending levels and extensive religious, mythological and secular sculpture.
empires.architectural_notes: Sun Temple, Modhera: The Suryakund reservoir precedes the Sabha Mandap. Steps and subsidiary shrines frame the water, while carved pillars mediate the approach toward the main shrine. Rani-ki-Vav: Stair flights descend through pillared levels toward the well. Sculptural panels line the walls, connecting structural rhythm, water access and ceremonial movement.

sources.title: Sun Temple, Modhera — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Nayakas of Madurai
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple: The Madurai complex developed around the shrines of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar and preserves important Nayak-period work. The district account emphasizes its sculptured pillars, paintings and musical stone supports; the building history cannot be reduced to one founding year.
empires.architectural_notes: Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple: Nested precincts and gateway towers surround the twin shrines. The Thousand Pillar Hall and processional corridors provide distinct architectural experiences within the living temple.

sources.title: Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple — historical and architectural reference

empires.name: Malla rulers of Bishnupur
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Rasmancha, Bishnupur: The Malla ruler Bir Hambir is credited with building the Rasmancha. It served as a ceremonial gathering place for images during the Ras festival.
empires.architectural_notes: Rasmancha, Bishnupur: Repeated arches surround the central chamber on a raised platform beneath a pyramidal roof.

empires.name: Karkota dynasty
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Martand Sun Temple: The ruined temple is attributed to Lalitaditya Muktapida in the eighth century in the institutional archaeological record. Its surviving architecture should be read as evidence of an incomplete structure rather than an intact reconstructed temple.
empires.architectural_notes: Martand Sun Temple: A monumental central shrine stands within a large colonnaded enclosure. Gateways, court space and framed mountain views organize the elevated site.

empires.name: Namgyal rulers of Ladakh
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Leh Palace: The nine-storey palace was built in the seventeenth century under Sengge Namgyal. The National Culture Fund documents its masonry, sun-dried bricks and timber.
empires.architectural_notes: Leh Palace: The stacked volumes rise in terraces against the ridge. Windows and projecting timber details break up the long elevations.

empires.name: Wadiyar rulers of Mysore
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Mysore Palace: The Wadiyar palace was rebuilt after a fire in 1897. Henry Irwin designed the present palace, completed in 1912.
empires.architectural_notes: Mysore Palace: Domed towers and arcades organize the main façade. The interior includes ceremonial halls and courtly spaces.

empires.name: Holkar rulers
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Kashi Vishwanath Temple: The official Kashi portal credits Ahilyabai Holkar with rebuilding the present temple in 1780. The date describes the principal shrine within a larger living sacred precinct.
empires.architectural_notes: Kashi Vishwanath Temple: The spired shrine sits within the dense historic setting of Varanasi and is linked to the ghats by the modern precinct route.

empires.name: Nawabs of Awadh
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Bara Imambara: Asaf-ud-Daula commissioned the imambara in 1784. Lucknow district records the building campaign in the context of famine relief.
empires.architectural_notes: Bara Imambara: A central vaulted hall is framed by subsidiary spaces, with passages above forming the Bhul Bhulaiya.

empires.name: Kachwaha rulers of Amber and Jaipur
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Amber Fort: The palace-fort developed through successive Kachwaha building campaigns, beginning under Man Singh I in 1592. Its external defensive character contrasts with decorated interiors and ceremonial halls in sandstone and marble. Hawa Mahal: Sawai Pratap Singh commissioned the palace façade in 1799. Its characteristic screened windows form part of Jaipur’s historic urban architecture and allowed views of street activity from within the palace. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur: Sawai Jai Singh II commissioned the observatory in the early eighteenth century. Its architectural instruments were built to observe celestial positions.
empires.architectural_notes: Amber Fort: Monumental gates enter the Jaleb Chowk and subsequent palace courts. Public and private halls, mirrored spaces and views toward Maota Lake structure the visitor’s movement. Hawa Mahal: A vertically layered street elevation is articulated by many small projecting windows. The façade’s light and air-filtering openings are its primary architectural focus. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur: Fixed structures align to the sky. The Samrat Yantra uses a sloping gnomon and graduated quadrants to measure local solar time.

empires.name: Rulers of Mewar
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Chittorgarh Fort: Chittorgarh is part of the serial Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscription. Its long history includes successive phases of occupation and major Rajput building campaigns. Kumbhalgarh Fort: Rana Kumbha is associated with the fifteenth-century fortifications at Kumbhalgarh. Later buildings within the walls belong to other phases.
empires.architectural_notes: Chittorgarh Fort: Ramparts follow the hilltop and enclose reservoirs, palaces, temples and commemorative towers. Kumbhalgarh Fort: Long ramparts follow the Aravalli ridges, with gates controlling approaches to the fortified interior.

empires.name: Rathore rulers of Marwar
empires.summary: Regional patronage, craftsmanship and changing monumental settings
empires.history: Mehrangarh Fort: Rao Jodha laid the foundation in 1459. The museum trust records major later phases under Rao Maldeo and Maharaja Ajit Singh.
empires.architectural_notes: Mehrangarh Fort: Walls crown a steep rock. The ascent leads through gates to palatial rooms and carved courtyard façades.
